description: Explore the internal architecture of plants, from growing root tips to the formation of wood.

slides.title: Welcome to Plant Anatomy
slides.content:
# Plant Anatomy

Welcome to Plant Anatomy! This is the study of the internal structure and tissues of plants. We will look at how plants are built from the inside out.

## What You Will Learn:
- **Meristematic Tissues** - Where plant growth happens
- **Permanent Tissues** - Simple and complex tissues
- **Xylem and Phloem** - The vascular system
- **Secondary Growth** - How trees get thicker

> **Fun Fact:** By looking at the anatomy of tree rings, scientists can determine not only the age of the tree but the exact climate conditions for every year it lived!

slides.title: Meristematic Tissue
slides.content:
# The Centers of Growth

Unlike animals, plants continue to grow throughout their entire life. This growth is localized in specific regions containing Meristematic Tissue.

## Characteristics:
- Composed of actively dividing, undifferentiated cells.
- Cells have thin walls, dense cytoplasm, and lack vacuoles.

## Types based on location:
1. **Apical Meristems:** Located at the very tips of roots and shoots. Responsible for primary growth (increasing the **length** of the plant).
2. **Lateral Meristems:** Located parallel to the sides of the stem/root. Responsible for secondary growth (increasing the **girth/thickness** of the plant, like wood). E.g., Vascular cambium.
3. **Intercalary Meristems:** Located at the base of leaves or internodes (common in grasses). Allows cut grass to quickly regrow.

slides.title: Simple Permanent Tissues
slides.content:
# Simple Permanent Tissues

Once meristematic cells mature and stop dividing, they become permanent tissues. Simple tissues are made of only ONE type of cell.

## 1. Parenchyma:
- The most common tissue. Thin-walled, living cells.
- Forms the bulk of the plant body.
- Function: Photosynthesis (if they have chloroplasts, called chlorenchyma), storage of food, and secretion.

## 2. Collenchyma:
- Living cells with walls thickened at the corners (due to pectin and cellulose).
- Function: Provides flexible mechanical support to growing parts (like the stem of a young plant or the stalk of a leaf).

## 3. Sclerenchyma:
- Dead cells at maturity! Walls are extremely thick and highly lignified.
- Function: Purely mechanical support and rigidity. (Forms the hard shells of nuts and the grit in pears).

slides.title: Complex Permanent Tissues: Xylem
slides.content:
# The Vascular System: Xylem

Complex tissues are made of MORE THAN ONE type of cell working together. The vascular tissues are the plant's plumbing.

## Xylem (Water Transport):
- Conducts water and dissolved minerals upwards from roots to leaves.
- Most of the cells are DEAD and lignified to form strong, hollow pipes.

## Elements of Xylem:
1. **Tracheids:** Long, elongated dead cells with tapering ends. Present in all vascular plants.
2. **Vessels:** Long, cylindrical tube-like structures made of many cells fused end-to-end. (Primarily found in Angiosperms, making them highly efficient at moving water).
3. **Xylem Fibers:** Sclerenchyma cells for support.
4. **Xylem Parenchyma:** The only living cells in the xylem! Used for storage.

slides.title: Complex Permanent Tissues: Phloem
slides.content:
# The Vascular System: Phloem

## Phloem (Food Transport):
- Conducts synthesized food (sugars) from the leaves to all other parts of the plant (bidirectional flow).
- Most of the cells are LIVING.

## Elements of Phloem (in Angiosperms):
1. **Sieve Tube Elements:** Long, tube-like living cells placed end-to-end. Their end walls are perforated (sieve plates). Strangely, they lack a nucleus at maturity!
2. **Companion Cells:** Specialized parenchyma cells closely associated with sieve tubes. Because sieve tubes have no nucleus, the companion cell's nucleus controls the functions of BOTH cells.
3. **Phloem Parenchyma:** Used for storage.
4. **Phloem Fibers:** Sclerenchyma cells for support (the only dead cells in phloem. Jute and flax fibers are phloem fibers).

slides.quizQuestion: Which of the following cell types in the phloem is living but lacks a nucleus at maturity?

slides.title: Tissue Systems
slides.content:
# The Three Tissue Systems

All the tissues in a plant are organized into three main systems.

## 1. Epidermal Tissue System:
- The outer protective covering (epidermis).
- Covered by a waxy cuticle to prevent water loss.
- Contains **Stomata** (pores) guarded by guard cells for gas exchange.
- Contains root hairs (for water absorption) and trichomes (stem hairs).

## 2. Ground Tissue System:
- All tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles.
- Forms the bulk of the plant (cortex, pith, mesophyll in leaves).
- Mostly made of parenchyma.

## 3. Vascular Tissue System:
- Contains the Xylem and Phloem bundles.

slides.title: Secondary Growth
slides.content:
# How Trees Grow Wide

Primary growth (apical meristem) makes plants taller. Secondary growth makes them thicker.

## The Vascular Cambium:
- A cylinder of lateral meristematic tissue located between the primary xylem and primary phloem in dicot stems.
- As it divides, it produces **Secondary Xylem** towards the INSIDE and **Secondary Phloem** towards the OUTSIDE.
- The massive accumulation of Secondary Xylem over years is what we call **WOOD**.
- The older, inner wood becomes blocked with resins and dies (Heartwood - dark and strong). The newer, outer wood remains active in transporting water (Sapwood - lighter in color).

Because growth slows down in winter and speeds up in spring, the secondary xylem forms distinct annual **Tree Rings**!

slides.title: Summary: Plant Anatomy
slides.content:
# Summary

## Key Concepts Reviewed:

- **Meristems:** Apical (primary growth/length) and Lateral (secondary growth/thickness).
- **Simple Tissues:** Parenchyma (bulk/storage), Collenchyma (flexible support), Sclerenchyma (dead, rigid support).
- **Xylem:** Conducts water UP. Mostly dead cells. Tracheids and highly efficient Vessels.
- **Phloem:** Conducts food everywhere. Mostly living cells. Sieve tubes (no nucleus) controlled by Companion cells.
- **Tissue Systems:** Epidermal (outer protection, stomata), Ground (bulk filler), Vascular (plumbing).
- **Secondary Growth:** Vascular cambium produces secondary xylem inwards (forming Wood and tree rings) and secondary phloem outwards.

> **Congratulations!** You have completed the Plant Anatomy module.
